title: Deliver completion advices without losing or reordering them

blocks.text: Completions (0220 advices) report purchases that have already happened, so they must reach the host, however long that takes. This SAF keeps them in a database table, the `Store` at the bottom of `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AdviceSaf.java`, instead of a Space queue. The ideas of 12.7 still apply. Only the tools are different: the table has `oldest`, `update`, `delete` and `insert`, and no `push`.

Finish the four places marked `TODO`. `sendOldest` is called again and again by a single sender. When you're done, an advice survives a process that dies while sending it, goes out as a repeat after an unanswered attempt, and never lets a later advice overtake it. About 10 lines in total.
The tests simulate a crash by giving `sendOldest` a MUX that throws in the middle of `request`, then building a new `AdviceSaf` on the same table.

cases.says: answered advices leave the table and reach the host oldest first
an advice stays stored while it is being sent, so a process that dies mid-send loses nothing
an unanswered advice stays at the front of the line, so a later advice never overtakes it
every attempt after an unanswered one goes out as a repeat, 0221
any answer means the host has seen the advice, whatever field 39 says
nothing is sent while the link is down, and an advice that never went out is not a repeat

origin.section: 12.7 A Reversal Must Outlive the Process and Wait Its Turn

concepts: A store-and-forward queue keeps a message stored while it is sent, repeats it only after a real attempt, keeps its place, and counts any answer as delivery.
